title.narrative: Agricultural Value Chain Competitiveness and Safety

description.narrative: The project will strengthen value chains of competitive agricultural products (CAPs) cassava, mangoes, cashew nuts, vegetables, and native chicken in the provinces of Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Siem Reap, and Tboung Khmum. The project will (i) facilitate access to credit for agro-enterprises and agricultural cooperatives; (ii) promote viable market links among agro-enterprises and agricultural cooperatives, and enhance food safety and quality; and (iii) improve farm-to-market connectivity. The project will benefit 230 agricultural cooperatives (about 27,000 households) and about 50 agribusinesses in the project areas, and the number of beneficiaries will be expanded through intermediary financing.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Agricultural value chain connectivity enhanced Indicator: About 3,000 road safety training participants, of which at least 50% are female, reported increased knowledge on the subject (baseline: 0, 0%). Achievement: 4479 Progress/Status: Road safety training is completed in six target provinces, namely, Preah Vihear, Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, Tboung Khmum, Siem Reap, and Oddar Meanchey with 4,479 participants, of which 2,276 are women (51%) reported increased knowledge after training from 56% at the pre-test to 88% at the post-test. Among them, it was reported that women increased knowledge after the training from 55% at the pre-test to 89% at the post-test. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain connectivity enhanced Indicator: At least 130 km of farm-to-market roads improved and climate-proofed to enhance connectivity between farms and markets (2020 baseline: 0 km). (RFI B) Achievement: 115.5 Progress/Status: The rehabilitation of 115.55 km of farm-to-market roads (FMRs) across the six target provinces has been completed, achieving 100% physical progress.
The Ministry of Rural Development (MRD) signed a contract with the selected contractor for additional FMRs totaling 25.24 km in January 2026 with the valued of $4,741,039.88.
The Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) and Social Due Diligence Report (DDR) for the 25.24 km of additional FMRs commenced in Q3 2025 and are expected to be completded and approved very soon. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least $40 million in AVC loans and equity capital loans provided to eligible borrowers, of which at least 25% ($10.0 million) is provided to women-owned PAEs and female borrowers (female farmers) (2020 baseline: $0, 0%) Achievement: 13748738 Progress/Status: Loans have been disbursed to 823 sub-borrowers, amounting to a total of $18,881,731.88, representing 47.2% of the total loan allocation of $40 million.
Of this amount, Sathapana Bank (SPNB) disbursed $11,614,231.88 to 693 sub-borrowers, while ARDB disbursed $7,267,500 to 130 sub-borrowers.
Loans disbursed to women sub-borrowers totaled $8,167,356, equivalent to 20.42% of the total loan allocation and 43.25% of the total amount disbursed. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least 40% of AVC loan recipients are micro, small and medium-sized PAEs (2020 baseline: 0) (RFI A) Achievement: 14 Progress/Status: Of the 823 sub-loans disbursed, 146 were provided to participating agro-enterprises (PAEs). Of these, 145 sub-loans were extended to micro, small, and medium PAEs, representing 17.62% of total sub-borrowers and 99.31% of all PAE sub-borrowers. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least 50 government and PFI staff, of which at least 25% are female, report increased knowledge on AVC financing and credit guarantee and green financing (2020 baseline: 0, 0%) Achievement: 433 Progress/Status: A total of 485 participants from government agencies and participating financial institutions (PFIs) have enhanced their knowledge of agricultural value chain (AVC) financing and credit guarantee mechanisms. Among them, 91 participants (18.8%) are women. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: About 230 PACs established IBPs with PAEs, of which at least 20% of PACs established contract farming arrangements or other alternative arrangements such as seasonal sales agreement (2020 baseline: 0, 0%) Progress/Status: 27 new contracts in 2025. 43 PACs have signed a total of 70 contract farming or sales agreements with two PAEs, six companies, and one collector.
11 IBP forums: 40 letters of intent (IBP Agreements) have been signed between PACs and PAEs.
Detailed engineering drawings (DEDs) and bills of quantity (BOQs) for 120 small infrastructure structures have been completed. These were divided into three procurement lots. Bids have been received and are currently under review. Contracts are expected to be signed in Q1 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 10 PAEs obtained food safety assurance certificates (2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: While several companies have expressed interest in certification, many are unwilling or unable to finance the required factory upgrades, which can cost approximately $20,000, particularly given the limited availability of long-term financing. Meetings held in July confirmed that ADB and MEF do not permit direct financing of private company facilities, which has constrained private sector interest in certification.
In response, the recent ADB review mission proposed the introduction of basic-level certifications—such as ISO 22000, 5S, and CODEX food safety certification—as an initial step toward compliance with food safety standards. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 30% of cassava PACs adopted disease cleaned materials and at least 30% of mango and cashew PACs adopted improved crop production practices and techniques and at least 30% of poultry farms adopted improved breeds, including at least 30% overall participation of women farmers (2020 baseline: 0%, 0%, 0%) Progress/Status: 10,000 disease-cleaned stems have been transferred from CARDI to DOIC for multiplication. (over 500,000 stems needed). CARDI is expected to distribute improved chili and cherry tomato varieties seeds to farmers by 2027. The recent ADB review mission recommended that CARDI consider two additional high-demand vegetable crops and begin developing improved genetic materials for farmer distribution.
Nine off-season mango demonstrations and 28 cashew demonstrations focusing on best cultivation practices were initiated. Cassava demonstrations were delayed until Q1 2026 due to the missed planting season in 2025. Demonstrations will continue over two seasons.
GDAHP are supporting four commercial chick-breeders to supply cross-breed chicks. Four chicken shed constructions have been completed. Contracts between cross-breeders and chick raisers were signed with GDAHP in Q4 2025.
Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 350 farmers (PAC members), of which at least 60% are women, obtained CamGAP certificates (2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: A total of 300 farmers (PAC members) have applied for CamGAP certification. Of these, the Department of Plant Protection, Sanitary and Phyto- Sanitary Department (DPPSPS), General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) has screened, inspected, and audited 150 farmers from 30 PACs across the six former target provinces. These 150 farmers have been certified and are expected to receive their CamGAP certificates in Q1 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: Integrated ICT data platform with geo-tagged farm level information built (baseline in 2020: None) Progress/Status: MAFF's digitalization strategic plan has been approved by MAFF Minister on 26 July 2024.
An updated procurement plan will be submitted to ADB by the end of Q1 2026. An ICT consultant is being recruited to revise the packages in consultation with AIDOC. Procurement of end-user computers is ongoing, and an IT consultant is being recruited (support date center). Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:
Value addition of five competitive agricultural value chains in the project areas increased

Products of at least 40 vegetable and/or poultry PACs sold their products at modern retail markets Progress/Status: 164 PACs have been selected as direct beneficiaries, with many involved in vegetable and poultry production.
Training on CamGAP and food safety standards has been provided to farmers and agro-enterprises, which is a prerequisite for accessing modern retail markets. Linking small producers to modern retail outlets is also a considerable leap. It is suggested, even at this stage, that the potential to achieve outcomes will need careful monitoring.
Some PAEs in the target provinces are selling their vegetables and/or chickens to modern retail markets (no quantitative data yet) Data Source: d. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:

Volume of cassava starch production increased to at least 150,000 tons per annum Progress/Status: CARDI has initiated multi-site experiments in five provinces to identify mosaic virus-resistant cassava varieties, and has produced 2,000 disease-free stems via tissue culture, with plans to produce 8,000 more in 2025. Due to limited production capacity, commercial sources will be needed to meet the demand for demonstration farms, which require over 500,000 stems. Based on deep assessment conducted by DAI from March to July 2025, one PAE namely Seung Kimheng Cassava Starch Enterprise is processing cassava starch 50 to 60 tons daily. Data Source: c. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:

Volume of processed cashew increased to at least 15,000 tons per annum Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: This target is likely to be met.
Foundational activities are underway, including the establishment of inclusive business partnerships (IBPs) and contract farming arrangements between PACs and cashew processing companies.
Demonstration farms for cashew cultivation have been planned, with cashew demos has started since Q3 2025.
Based on deep assessment conducted by DAI from March to July 2025, 2,529 tons of cashew nut has been processed by the 14 selected PAEs in 2025. Data Source: a. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs

Volume of processed mango increased to at least 20,000 tons per annum Progress/Status: Demonstration farms for mango cultivation started in Q3 2025.
No PAEs process mangoes in the target provinces.
Mango prices have fallen, markets have been lost due to international competition and new markets are not available. Cambodian SPS facilities are not at international standard. Data Source: b. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:
